correctness.rationale: The finite cube map of the smooth irreducible Klein quadric is an integral hypersurface with explicitly derived irreducible degree-six equation. The plane cubic has exactly one nondegenerate node; exhaustive coordinate-product cases yield one CI(2,2) threefold and three smooth quadrics with no hidden singular support. The CI is prime by saturated torus lattice, boundary dimension and CM reducedness. Generic node and A2 completed germs follow from the Hessian and local unit absorption. The 27-element subgroup gives a finite birational normal quotient. verify.py independently checks symbolic identities, parameter rank, stabilizer count, and full projective F5/F7 point enumerations; finite fields only corroborate the symbolic characteristic-zero proof.

value.rationale: The original geometric increment identifies the entire stratified singular support of a natural coordinatewise power of the smallest Plücker Grassmannian, including a sharp normality failure along an irreducible degree-four divisor and three distinct higher-codimension A2 strata, plus its finite normal quotient. This is more than a numerical degree exercise or a rephrasing of the general norm polynomial: it separates divisorial double-branch behavior from the exceptional quadratic surfaces, and contrasts structurally with the different square-power model.
